chunks: Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Sulaiman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a Magian's dog that a Muslim man takes, then mentions the name of Allah when he releases it: may he eat what it catches for him?
He عليه السلام said: “Yes, because it is trained, and the name of Allah has been mentioned upon it.”

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ: what the dog catches or seizes
key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ: the name of Allah recited over the act
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ الْمُسْلِمُ: the Muslim man who takes and uses the dog for hunting
key_terms.حِينَ يُرْسِلُهُ: at the time he sends the dog out
key_terms.فَيُسَمِّي: he mentions the name of Allah
key_terms.كَلْبِ الْمَجُوسِيِّ: the dog belonging to a Magian

ai.seo_question: Is game caught by a Magian's trained dog halal if a Muslim releases it with the name of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning hunting with a trained dog originally belonging to a Magian. It indicates that if a Muslim takes the dog and mentions the name of Allah when sending it, then the game it catches is permissible to eat because the dog is trained and tasmiyah has been performed.
